To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

there were no significant differences in the metabolic and hormonal responses of sleep deprived individuals exposed to cold air for 180-min compared with those of individuals exposed to cold after a night of normal sleep.
sleep deprivation combined with 12°C cold air exposure did not significantly affect the hormonal and metabolic stress response.
the hormonal and metabolic response to cold exposure was not significantly different when compared with a normal night of restful sleep.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physiological effects of sleep deprivation and the effects of sleep deprivation on physiological stress.
the effects of sleep deprivation (SD) on the hormonal and metabolic response to cold.
the effect of sleep deprivation (SD) on the human body’s physiological responses to cold stress.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SDEP and cold exposure combined were not enough of an environmental stressor to cause significant changes in hormonal and metabolic responses in the participants.
cold exposure does not have an effect on the hormonal responses to SDEP.
the hormonal and metabolic response to cold exposure was similar in both the normal sleep group and the SDEP group.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SDEP combined and/or followed by cold exposure does not elicit a differential response in these hormonal and metabolic parameters.
SDEP does not appear to have a great effect on the hormonal and metabolic response to cold exposure.
SDEP and cold exposure may not be additive stressors, at least in terms of the hormonal and metabolic changes we assessed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cold stress did not appear to exacerbate the hormonal and metabolic changes associated with sleep deprivation.
the combination of SDEP and cold exposure did not cause a differential response of the hormonal and metabolic variables studied.
SDEP combined protracted cold exposure is not a great enough environmental stressor to elicit a differential response in hormonal and metabolic parameters.
